title: 9/11 and the War on Terror

cards.h: The morning the world's news changed
cards.b:
On 11 September 2001, nineteen hijackers took four planes. Two struck the Twin Towers of the World Trade Center, one hit the Pentagon, and one crashed in a field in Pennsylvania after passengers fought back. Nearly 3,000 people died.

It was the deadliest terror attack in history, and it launched two long wars.

The attack was carried out by al-Qaeda, led by Osama bin Laden, who had base camps in Afghanistan under the Taliban. Al-Qaeda had grown from the anti-Soviet war in Afghanistan in the 1980s.

It had already struck US embassies in Kenya and Tanzania (1998).
The US toppled the Taliban in weeks. In March 2003 it invaded Iraq, saying Saddam Hussein had weapons of mass destruction. None were found.

The 'War on Terror' brought the Patriot Act, the Guantanamo prison and drone strikes. Bin Laden was found and killed by US forces at Abbottabad in Pakistan on 2 May 2011.

In August 2021, after 20 years, US troops left Afghanistan and the Taliban retook Kabul on 15 August.

Hundreds of thousands died directly in the wars, with estimates varying by study. Millions were displaced. The Iraq war also helped create the space where ISIS grew.

Terrorism continued in many countries, and debates about security and freedom reshaped airports and laws.

Myth: Iraq was behind the attacks.Fact: investigations (including the 9/11 Commission) found no operational link between Saddam's Iraq and the attacks. The WMD claim also proved false.

Also: the Taliban's regime was separate from al-Qaeda, though it hosted it.

Five things to remember

  1. 9/11 killed nearly 3,000.
  2. Al-Qaeda under bin Laden planned it.
  3. The US invaded Afghanistan (2001) and Iraq (2003).
  4. The Taliban retook Kabul in August 2021.
  5. India had also faced major attacks.

Think about it

  • How should states balance security and liberty?
  • Why is defining terrorism so hard?
